clue.text: Miss flying west in Romania, crashing

indicators.note: something crashing breaks up, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for west on a compass

explanation.surface: An aircraft heading west over Romania goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link word here. The letters W and ROMANIA together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A miss is a woman, and one who is flying an aircraft is a female pilot.

clue.text: Complete transformation of triangle

indicators.note: a transformation changes a thing's form, so the letters of the next word are reshaped

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson in which a triangle is completely changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something integral is whole and entire, lacking no part.

clue.text: Apply oneself at school acquiring good C or D

parts.note: to apply oneself is to work hard

indicators.note: the phrase for being at school takes in the letter for good, so it goes inside

parts.note: being at school during lessons is being in class

explanation.surface: Advice to study hard and get a decent grade, a C or a D.
explanation.walkthrough: C and D look like exam grades, but they are British social grades: the classification runs A, B, C1, C2, D, E, and C2 and D cover manual workers.
explanation.definitionFit: In British market-research social grading, groups C2 and D are the skilled and semi-skilled manual workers.

clue.text: Courage of London police let out

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Police, London's police force

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the short word are put out of order

explanation.surface: Bravery shown by the London police when they release someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle is spirit and pluck, the strength of character to face difficulty.

clue.text: New trouble to fix

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A fresh problem needs repairing.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something in place is to fasten it, for example with a hammered pin.

clue.text: I allow small number inside without knowledge

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviated number within the word for allow

parts.note: to grant is to allow or permit
No. is the short form of number

explanation.surface: Someone letting a small number in without knowing anything about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ignorant is to lack information or awareness.

clue.text: One peccadillo's overturned condition of divorce

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a peccadillo is a minor sin

explanation.surface: A single small misdeed leads to a divorce being ruled on.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of peccadillo's is a link meaning 'is'. In English law a decree nisi is the provisional order before a divorce becomes final.
explanation.definitionFit: Decree nisi is the conditional stage of a divorce, nisi being Latin for unless.

clue.text: In variety show, rare song often performed

indicators.note: variety means a mixture, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A variety show features a song that is seldom heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety show' looks like a single phrase, but 'In variety' is the anagram signal and SHOW and RARE are the letters mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A warhorse is a familiar piece performed so often it has become a staple.

clue.text: One giving financial support to London arts centre gets decoration

parts.note: an angel is a backer who funds a theatrical show
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London

explanation.surface: A theatre backer is given an honour by a London arts venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied green stems of this plant are used to decorate cakes and desserts.

clue.text: Top performer sings with backing

indicators.note: backing signals the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing on someone, which is to rat

explanation.surface: A leading performer sings with a backing group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link; 'backing' looks like backing vocals but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The headline act or leading actor in a show is its celebrity name.

clue.text: Boiler getting detached makes a mess

parts.note: a boiler can be a vessel for boiling water, such as a kettle
someone detached is aloof, standoffish

explanation.surface: A domestic boiler coming loose causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boiler' suggests a central-heating unit, but here it is anything that boils water.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretty kettle of fish is an idiom for an awkward or muddled situation.

clue.text: I sign draft re revised parliamentary procedure

indicators.note: a revised text has been altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician agreeing to sign a revised draft of a parliamentary rule.
explanation.definitionFit: The first formal stage of a bill's passage through parliament is its introduction to the House.

clue.text: Royal person included in newspapers

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for newspapers

parts.note: newspapers collectively are the press
inc. is the abbreviation for included or inclusive

explanation.surface: A royal figure features in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' reads as one phrase, but 'included' gives INC and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A king's or queen's daughter is a member of the royal family.

clue.text: Upstart harbours display of petulance

annotationWithheld.why: 'Upstart harbours display of petulance (5)': STROP is PORTS (harbours) turned 'up' in a down clue, but 'Upstart' is one printed word, so 'start' is left with no job and the reversal signal cannot be cut out of it

clue.text: Better ventilated zone by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase tells the solver the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a zone is an area

explanation.surface: Someone says a district is breezier than it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words are pronounced almost alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere better ventilated has more fresh air flowing through it.

clue.text: Group of countries in Arab locality

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An alliance of nations within the Arab region.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of nations acting together politically.

clue.text: Horse-drawn coach makes bishop rather unwell by morning

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
feeling rough is feeling rather ill
a.m. stands for the morning hours

explanation.surface: A carriage ride leaves the bishop feeling queasy by morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A brougham is a light four-wheeled closed carriage pulled by one horse.

clue.text: The Queen entering American university gets high mark

indicators.note: entering means the abbreviation for the Queen goes inside the university

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: The monarch visits an American university and earns a top grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A merit is a grade awarded for good work, above a pass.

clue.text: Chap handin' out instrument

parts.note: a chap is a man
handing out is doling, and the clue drops the final G just as the piece does

explanation.surface: A fellow casually distributing something, presumably musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in handin' is the clue's way of dropping the G from doling.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandolin is a stringed instrument of the lute family, played with a plectrum.

clue.text: Record and intercept communication (electronic)

parts.note: to tap a phone line is to intercept its messages
E is the usual abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Bugging electronic messages and recording them.
explanation.definitionFit: To tape something is to record it on magnetic tape.

clue.text: Delightful lake in rustic surrounding

indicators.note: surrounding means the country dweller goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: a rustic is a country person, a peasant
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A charming lake set in countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rustic' reads as an adjective, but here it is the noun, a country dweller.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pleasant is agreeable and enjoyable.

clue.text: Make a priest confused in road

indicators.note: confused signals the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bewildered priest-maker out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to confer holy orders, admitting someone to the priesthood.

clue.text: Wizard journalist made erratic progress

parts.note: Harry Potter is the boy wizard of J. K. Rowling's books
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A wizard reporter wandered about aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to move about in a leisurely, aimless way.

clue.text: Make false turn at bunker

indicators.note: to make something false is to falsify or distort it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer takes a wrong turn at a sand trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunker' suggests golf, but it means one who bunks off, as from school.
explanation.definitionFit: To bunk off is British slang for skipping school, so a bunker is one who stays away.

clue.text: Hides what sports fan does before match

definitions.meaning: to hide is to take cover and disappear from view

definitions.text: what sports fan does before match
definitions.meaning: a fan travels to the stadium before the game, literally heading for the ground

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally: a ground is a sports stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: To take cover like a hunted fox going into its earth is the idiom's sense of hiding.

clue.text: Aristocrat and paragon, beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: a paragon or prized example is a pearl

explanation.surface: A nobleman, a model of virtue, is executed.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a nobleman ranking above viscount and below marquess.

clue.text: Lecherously eye up for a dance

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to leer is to look at someone lecherously

explanation.surface: Someone ogles another at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish folk dance.

clue.text: Russian — one near front

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
the van is the leading part of an army, near the front

explanation.surface: A Russian stationed close to the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is the typical Russian man's name, used as slang for a Russian.

clue.text: A warrior going round is flipping rough

indicators.note: the warrior goes round the turned word, enclosing it

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior

indicators.note: flipping signals the short word is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A fighter spinning about is really coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reads as a mild expletive but reverses IS to SI, which goes inside BRAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrasive is harsh and grating, like sandpaper or a brusque manner.

clue.text: Take up a case set down by one departure point

parts.note: to be set down from a vehicle is to alight, past tense lit
the Roman numeral for one is I
passengers depart from an airport gate

explanation.surface: A traveller drops off a suitcase at the boarding gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests luggage at an airport, but here it is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To litigate is to take a dispute to court.
